main_issue: Whether Agent D can keep showering and cooking at 4:45 a.m. daily, or must reduce the noise (e.g., do it the night before) for the others' sleep and work or study.

A-B.evidence: A and B both raise their own needs (turns 3, 4) and both ask D for night-before accommodation (turns 6, 9). They never address each other.

A-C.evidence: Both are bothered by D's noise (turns 3, 12) and both end up accepting D's partial concessions (turns 8, 28). They never address each other.

A-D.evidence: A asks for Sunday-night prep (turn 6). D agrees to shower the night before (turn 7) and A thanks D (turn 8), so they reach agreement.

B-C.evidence: Both want less noise from D (turns 9, 12). They don't address each other, and B's final position is unclear.

B-D.evidence: B asks for night-before showers on Monday and Wednesday (turn 9). D refuses: 'I can't also give up my shower' (turn 10). B's narrowed request for Wednesday (turn 11) goes unmet, and D holds to one night (turn 13).

C-D.evidence: C objects to the daily wake-ups (turns 12, 18). D refuses to give up the shower (turn 22). C then concedes: 'if you have to shower, be quick' (turn 23). D agrees (turn 27) and C thanks D (turn 31). The core objection is not resolved.
